children: With vehicle exports rising 24 per cent to 20,312 units in FY2024-25, Isuzu is strengthening India’s place in its global operations

Isuzu Motors India is looking to build on its recent business growth while expanding India’s role as a manufacturing and export base for the Japanese automaker. The company recorded 2.5 times profitable growth last year, while exports rose 24 per cent to 20,312 vehicles in FY2024-25.

Rajesh Mittal, President and Managing Director of Isuzu Motors India, in an exclusive conversation with Utkarsh Agarwal, Editorial Lead of BW Auto World, discusses the markets driving Isuzu’s exports, how the company plans to strengthen its presence in India, and why local suppliers must meet global quality standards. He also explains what will determine the future of electric pickups in India, where charging infrastructure and the readiness of the commercial vehicle market remain key considerations.
As Isuzu looks to expand its international business, India’s ability to serve both domestic customers and overseas markets will be central to its next phase of growth.
Read the edited excerpts below

Q. As a Japanese company operating in India, what are the biggest lessons Isuzu has learnt from Indian customers and market, and how have those lessons influenced the way you develop products globally?

India is an important market for Isuzu. Over the years, we have gained an understanding of how customer expectations evolve in a diverse and dynamic automotive market. The insights we gathered here have reinforced the importance of offering the right products, with proactive aftersales service, to ensure that they meet the demanding customer needs without compromising on Isuzu’s core values of quality, durability and reliability.
Over the last few years, Isuzu Motors India has witnessed a strong growth in business and operations, and this has resulted in a 2.5 times profitable growth last year.

Indian customers always expect the best for their intended purpose, and at the same time suits their value perception. The Isuzu D-Max V-Cross, India’s first Adventure Utility Vehicle, established a lifestyle pickup segment in India when it launched. Similarly, the response to our D-Max and S-Cab range reflects the varied expectations of customers, from business productivity to personal mobility.

From a global perspective, our experience in India reinforces the value of combining proven engineering capabilities with a deep understanding of local market requirements in offering products with a high degree of localisation. Our vehicles are manufactured using Isuzu Monozukuri and are built to meet global quality standards, ensuring consistent quality and reliability across markets.

Q. Isuzu India exported 20,312 vehicles in FY2024-25, registering 24 per cent growth over the previous year. What drove this performance, and which international markets offer the biggest opportunities for further growth?

In recent years, Isuzu Motors India has been among the leading commercial vehicle exporters and has been recognised with awards for the same. Today, our export markets include GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) and other neighbouring countries. Since 2019, we have been successful to secure and delight customers in the GCC region with robust product of global quality that Isuzu is known for. This underscores our ability to manufacture products that are Made-in-India that cater to diverse international market needs.
Our export performance in FY2024-25 is a reflection of steady expansion of our brand’s international footprint, and of India's growing role as a manufacturing base within Isuzu’s global operations.

We initially began exporting to Nepal in 2017, and later expanded to Bhutan and Bangladesh. One of the highlights is that IMI has also exported more than one lakh Made-in-India engines to Egypt. Going forward, these markets will remain important regions for our export business. We are also evaluating opportunities to expand, and will remain focused on building a sustainable business.

Q. In July 2026, Isuzu signed a five-year export agreement with Kamarajar Port. How will this partnership support your export plans, and is there scope to expand the range of vehicles and markets served from India?

Our five-year agreement with Kamarajar Port marks an important step in strengthening the logistics infrastructure that supports Isuzu’s export operations from India. The partnership is expected to facilitate the continued movement of vehicles manufactured at our Sri City facility in Andhra Pradesh to our export markets. The volume-linked concessional wharfage rates under the agreement will also support greater cost efficiency and provide a structured framework for our export operations over the next five years.

Our association with Kamarajar Port dates back to 2019, when we began using it to export our D-Max and S-Cab commercial vehicles to markets including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Jordan. The new agreement formalises this longstanding relationship and will act as a strong enabler for our international business.
Q. The Indian pickup market serves very different needs, from small businesses and fleet operators to lifestyle buyers. How do you see this market evolving?

The Indian pickup market is evolving rapidly, with customers increasingly looking for vehicles that offer versatility beyond a single purpose. Pickups are now finding relevance among a wider range of buyers who appreciate the ability of our vehicles to adapt to both professional and personal needs. They also appreciate the reliable and strong performance of the Isuzu range of vehicles.

Now-a-days, customers are actively seeking vehicles that offers connected solutions, better infotainment, higher safety and comfort along with more power and performance at an affordable cost. A significant set of commercial vehicles user still prefer diesel as an ideal option as they operate across different terrains with optimal operating cost.

We see customers using our vehicles to support their businesses, day-to-day operations and for other personal uses. Especially our CV product portfolio, including the D-Max and S-Cab range, addresses these diverse requirements.

Q. Isuzu showcased its D-Max battery-electric concept at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo in 2025. What is the company learning from the development of electric pickups globally, and what factors will determine when such technology becomes suitable for India?
Isuzu is working on developing multiple powertrains including BEV. Currently, the D-Max BEV is available for sale in select countries including the Nordic region.

In India, the EV market is growing for passenger vehicles. But, the pace of transition will depend on how the ecosystem develops, particularly in terms of supporting infrastructure. This is a very critical parameter for the traction of electric commercial vehicles which is still in the nascent stage. Currently, we do not offer an EV pick-up for sale in India. We will continue to assess market developments as the ecosystem matures.

Q. Isuzu’s global strategy towards 2030 includes expanding into connected services, autonomous driving and carbon-neutral transport solutions. Which of these areas could have the greatest relevance for the Indian market in the coming years?

Isuzu’s global ambitions reflect our commitment to evolving mobility needs through technological advancement, innovation and sustainable transport solutions. The relevance and adoption of these developments across markets will depend on local requirements and market readiness, and we continue to closely observe how these areas evolve.

Q. India has a strong supplier base and a growing manufacturing ecosystem. How much potential do you see to increase local sourcing and involve Indian suppliers more deeply in Isuzu’s global operations?

We firmly believe in India’s growing manufacturing ecosystem and it has been a key contributor that supports our business plan. Isuzu would never compromise on the quality of the parts or its consistency as it has a direct bearing on the brand value of quality and reliability.

The challenge has been to leverage the sourcing potential to develop parts locally of highest quality that meet our global standards. We work closely with our suppliers to ensure this. In the last three years, a majority of our suppliers have been producing parts with zero defects and the number keeps increasing. Isuzu Motors India has also been leveraging India’s potential for Isuzu’s global sourcing requirements.
Q. Looking ahead to 2030, what would you like Isuzu India to achieve in terms of domestic market presence, exports and its contribution to the global business?

Isuzu is a global organisation which is working on various alternate energy technologies for the varied needs and norms of various markets. For India, our focus will be to offer appropriate products that satisfy the needs of the customer in terms of acquisition, versatile performance and ownership experience, at the right juncture.

Our understanding of the demanding commercial vehicle customers has given us insights to constantly develop and bring products that gives a better value proposition with best-in-class features. Such robust products act as enablers for the progress of our customers’ business. We have also been continuously ramping the expansion of our network, making products and services more accessible to the customers.
As mentioned earlier, Isuzu Motors India has witnessed a strong growth in business and operations, and it has resulted in a 2.5 times profitable growth last year.

While there are challenges due to global geopolitical scenarios, we are becoming resilient to mitigate the extent of impact of such challenges. We will stay committed to India in making quality vehicles that are Made-in-India for India and the World. As part of Isuzu’s global strategy, India is a key Monozukuri manufacturing base for the domestic and the global markets of Isuzu.
